subject: Region anchoring control evidence and conditional failover plan
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <security@medicore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@medicore.com>, legal@medicore.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Region anchoring evidence + conditional failover questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning. Medicore is proceeding through our security gating for the pilot and we need a concise packet showing how you will:

- Demonstrate that EU customer data will be pinned to EU-hosted inference endpoints (anchoring control), and
- Describe exactly how a conditional failover to non-EU nodes would be triggered and what telemetry/controls exist around that temporary egress (duration, notification, logging, and ability to revoke).

Specifically, for procurement/legal we need:
1) A short diagram or proof-of-control document that shows network flows and where KV cache/temporary replication may occur.
2) A list of subprocessors involved in the EU path and the windows during which a temporary hop to another region might happen.
3) The SLAs/notifications for any transient cross-border processing (how Medicore will be notified, expected max duration, and rollback controls).

Can you provide this by EOW (Friday)? If you need a template, we can share our standard security annex.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Senior Security Engineer, Medicore Health
security@medicore.com

On behalf of Procurement/Legal: legal@medicore.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <security@medicore.com>, Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@medicore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region anchoring evidence + conditional failover questions

Hi Priya / Oliver,

Appreciate the clear ask. We can deliver a compact packet covering all three bullets — diagram, subprocessor roster, and the transient failover playbook.

Quick clarifications so we scope the packet correctly:
- Do you want details at the VM/instance level (IPs, AZ mapping) or is an architectural diagram + control descriptions sufficient for Medicore legal?
- For the subprocessor list, do you need historical activation timestamps (times when a subprocessor was used) or just the currently active roster and contractual regions?

We are attaching a preliminary diagram and the current subprocessor ledger for the EU anchoring flow. The failover runbook attached is a draft but should answer most of your playbook questions: notification hooks, TTL on temporary KV replication (60 minutes by default), and automatic rollback checks.

Attachments: region-anchoring-diagram.pdf; subprocessor-ledger-2027-07.csv; conditional-failover-runbook.md

If that looks good I can produce a redlined, one-page evidence summary for your legal team by Friday.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182
From: Oliver Reed <oliver.reed@medicore.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <security@medicore.com>
Cc: legal@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region anchoring evidence + conditional failover questions

Aditya — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments. A few follow-ups from our security review team (copying them on this thread):

- The diagram looks good. We need one small addition: mark the control plane boundaries where the KMS keys for EU data are used and confirm whether KMS operations ever transit through US-managed control plane instances.
- The runbook mentions a default 60-minute TTL on temporary KV replication. In our environment we require a max 30-minute transient window unless there is an explicit exec-level waiver. Can Redwood support a configurable TTL down to 15 minutes?
- For subprocessors, please include the onboarding date and the country flag per entry (we need to confirm any subprocessor that could introduce a non-EU hop).

Also, please include a sample notification payload (webhook or email) that we would receive when a transient hop is triggered — the payload should contain: reason, triggering host, start_time, expected_end_time, and a signed trace id we can mash into our audit logs.

Thanks — if you can get these changes by Thursday EOD we can proceed to legal intake.

—Oliver
Director, Platform Security, Medicore Health
oliver.reed@medicore.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: action items for Medicore evidence packet

Aditya — summarizing internal next steps per Oliver/Priya: please review and confirm timelines.

1) KMS control-plane mapping: Engineering to confirm if any KMS handshakes for EU keys touch US control-plane services. Owner: Kim (me). ETA: 48 hours.
2) TTL configurability: Product/Runtime team to confirm whether KV transient TTL can be set to as low as 15 minutes and exposed as a customer-configurable parameter. Owner: Marissa (product ops) + Runtime Eng. ETA: 72 hours.
3) Subprocessor ledger augmentation: Add onboarding date and run a country flag column export. Owner: Aditya (liaison) + Legal Ops. ETA: 24 hours.
4) Notification payload example: Security/webhooks team to provide a sample JSON payload including signed trace_id and remediation link. Owner: Security Eng (internal) — Kim to request. ETA: 48 hours.

I'll coordinate with Runtime Eng and Security to get the answers. Once we have confirmation we'll produce the one-page evidence summary for Medicore legal.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
